ai.literal: Divisions having been complete, injury not fearing victorious army, king's among wealths all, head.
ai.translation: A victorious army, complete in its divisions and fearless of wounds, is the foremost of all a king's treasures.
ai.modern: எல்லா உறுப்புகளும் முழுமையாக அமைந்து, போரில் ஏற்படும் காயங்களுக்குப் பயப்படாத வெற்றி பெறும் படையே ஒரு அரசனின் செல்வங்கள் எல்லாவற்றிலும் முதன்மையானதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet identifies a strong military as the greatest asset of a ruler. The word 'உறுப்பு' refers to the essential divisions or components that make up a complete and well-rounded military force. 'ஊறு அஞ்சா' highlights the crucial psychological trait of the soldiers, meaning they do not fear physical injury or harm in battle. Because such a 'வெல்படை' (victorious army) protects and secures the state, it is considered the 'தலை' (head or foremost) among all the 'வெறுக்கை' (treasures) a king can possess.

ai.literal: In the time of ruin, injury not-fearing courage, in the time of defeat, to the ancient army except, is rare.
ai.translation: The courage that does not fear injury even in the face of ruin is rare to find except in a veteran army.
ai.modern: அழிவு வந்த காலத்திலும் காயங்களுக்கு அஞ்சாத வீரம், போரில் தோற்கும் நிலை வந்தாலும், தொன்றுதொட்டு வரும் பழைய படைக்கு அல்லாமல் மற்றவர்களுக்கு இருப்பது அரிது.
ai.explanation: This couplet praises the resilience of a veteran army. The word 'உலைவிடத்து' refers to a situation of ruin or collapse, while 'தொலைவிடத்து' means a state of defeat. Even in such dire circumstances, the 'வன்கண்' (courage) that does not fear 'ஊறு' (injury or wounds) is a unique trait. The poet asserts that such steadfast bravery is rare ('அரிது') in any force other than an ancient, well-established army ('தொல்படை').

ai.literal: If roared what will become ocean rat-army cobra when breathing will perish.
ai.translation: What does it matter if an army of rats roars like the ocean? It will perish the moment a cobra hisses.
ai.modern: எலிகளின் படை கடல் போல முழங்கினாலும் என்ன பயன்? ஒரு நாகப்பாம்பு மூச்சு விட்டாலே அந்தப் படை அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts a massive but weak army with a single, powerful warrior. The word உவரி (ocean) illustrates the sheer volume and loud noise of the rat army (எலிப்பகை). However, என்னாம் (what is the use) questions their strength, because just as rats scatter and die when a cobra (நாகம்) merely breathes or hisses (உயிர்ப்ப), a weak army will be instantly destroyed by a truly fierce force.

ai.literal: Without destruction, not being corrupted, being, the courage that came through lineage - that indeed is an army.
ai.translation: A true army is one that suffers no ruin, cannot be corrupted, and possesses a hereditary tradition of fearless courage.
ai.modern: அழிவில்லாமலும், பகைவரிடம் விலைபோகாமலும் இருந்து, பரம்பரையாக வந்த வீரத்தைக் கொண்டிருப்பதே உண்மையான படையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the essential qualities of a great army. First, it must be resilient, facing no ruin or defeat. Second, it must be fiercely loyal, never allowing itself to be corrupted or secretly won over by the enemy. Finally, it must possess a deep-rooted, hereditary courage that has been passed down through generations. The word 'வன்கண்' can sometimes mean hard-heartedness, but in this military context, it specifically means fearless bravery.

ai.literal: Death having raged against even if comes, having united facing which stands strength, that indeed [is an] army.
ai.translation: A true army is that which has the strength to stand united and face even Death, should it advance upon them in a rage.
ai.modern: எமன் சினந்து தன் மேல் வந்தாலும், சிதறாமல் ஒன்றாகச் சேர்ந்து எதிர்த்து நிற்கும் வலிமை உடையதே சிறந்த படையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate courage and solidarity of a true army. The word 'கூற்று' (Death) represents the most terrifying and invincible foe imaginable. Even if Death itself were to advance upon them in fury, a great army will not scatter in fear. Instead, they will unite ('கூடி') and stand their ground ('எதிர் நிற்கும்'). The true mark of an army is this collective strength ('ஆற்றல்') to face certain doom without breaking ranks.

ai.literal: Valor and honor, excellent path-going, trustworthiness, saying four indeed protection to the army.
ai.translation: Valor, honor, following the excellent path of tradition, and trustworthiness—these four alone are the safeguard of an army.
ai.modern: வீரம், மானம், சிறந்த முன்னோர் வழியில் நடத்தல், நம்பகத்தன்மை ஆகிய இந்த நான்குமே ஒரு படைக்கு அரணாகும்.
ai.explanation: An army's true strength does not lie merely in its weapons or numbers, but in its moral and psychological foundation. This couplet identifies four essential qualities: valor in battle, a sense of honor, adherence to the noble traditions of predecessors, and trustworthiness. Together, these four virtues act as the ultimate safeguard and protective armor for any military force.

ai.translation: A true army is one that knows its capacity to withstand the battle that has come upon it, and advances by breaking through the enemy's vanguard.
ai.modern: தன் மேல் வந்த போரைத் தாங்கும் ஆற்றலை அறிந்து, பகைவரின் முன்னணிப் படையைத் தடுத்து முன்னேறிச் செல்வதே சிறந்த படையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the core strength of a capable army. The word 'தார்' can mean a garland, but in this military context, it specifically refers to the vanguard or the front line of the opposing force. A true army first understands its own capability ('தன்மை') to endure the battle that is forced upon it. With this tactical awareness, it successfully withstands the enemy's initial charge and continues to advance.

ai.translation: Even if it lacks fighting quality and strength, an army will command respect through its splendid martial appearance.

ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the psychological impact of a well-arrayed army. The words 'அடல் தகை' (fighting quality) and 'ஆற்றல்' (strength) refer to the actual combat capabilities of the troops. Even if an army is deficient in these real martial skills, it can still achieve 'பாடு' (greatness or respect) simply through its 'படைத்தகை' (splendid martial appearance or formation). The visual grandeur and disciplined array of an army can intimidate enemies and earn glory on its own.

ai.literal: Weakness and, un-departing resentment and, poverty and, if without, will conquer, the army.
ai.translation: An army will conquer if it is free from weakness, lingering resentment, and poverty.
ai.modern: படைவீரர்களிடம் மனத்தளர்ச்சி, நீங்காத வெறுப்பு, வறுமை ஆகிய மூன்றும் இல்லாவிட்டால் அந்தப் படை வெற்றி பெறும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet identifies three internal flaws that can destroy an army's effectiveness. 'சிறுமை' refers to weakness or a shrinking in numbers and spirit. 'செல்லாத் துனி' means a deep, lingering resentment or grievance among the soldiers. 'வறுமை' points to poverty or a lack of proper resources and pay. If an army is free from these three defects, it will naturally be victorious.

ai.literal: Firm soldiers abundantly it possesses even if, an army, head-men when absent, is nothing.
ai.translation: Even if an army possesses an abundance of steadfast soldiers, it is nothing without capable commanders.
ai.modern: போர்க்களத்தில் நிலைத்து நிற்கும் வீரர்களைப் பெருமளவில் கொண்டிருந்தாலும், அவர்களை வழிநடத்தும் சிறந்த தலைவர்கள் இல்லாவிட்டால் அந்தப் படை பயனற்றதாகிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute necessity of leadership in warfare. The term 'நிலைமக்கள்' refers to steadfast soldiers who courageously hold their ground in battle. However, even if an army has these brave troops in great abundance, it cannot succeed without 'தலைமக்கள்' or capable commanders to guide them. The final word 'இல்' (is nothing) starkly concludes that without proper leadership, the sheer number of good soldiers amounts to nothing.
